cards.explanation: The answer is to throw it down before Pharaoh. The LORD says to tell Aaron, “Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh…” Aaron is Moses’ brother (Exodus 7:2), and Pharaoh is Egypt’s king. No speech, no dance, just drop the stick, friends. Easiest job description I’ve ever heard, and I’ve stamped a crooked cookie or two in my day.

The answer is that Pharaoh calls his wise men and sorcerers. He “…called the wise men and sorcerers and magicians of Egypt…” He sees a staff turn into a serpent and his first move is to call for backup, friends. That's like hearing a strange noise from your car and calling your cousin who “knows cars.”

The answer is True. The text says, “Each one threw down his staff, and it became a serpent.” The wise men, sorcerers and magicians did the same things by their magic arts (Exodus 7:11). Staffs turning into serpents, and then more staffs turning into serpents, friends. I would have needed a minute to sit down.

The answer is that Aaron's staff swallows them up. “But Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs.” Every magician threw down a staff, and one serpent was left standing. I’d have been counting my fingers afterward just to be sure I still had all of them.

The answer is hardened. “Still, Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.” Pharaoh is Egypt’s king, and he had just seen Aaron’s staff swallow up the other staffs. That's a lot to see and still not listen, friends. I'd have been asking for a replay, and his mind was already made up.

The answer is on the bank of the Nile. The LORD tells Moses, “Wait on the bank of the Nile to meet him…” Pharaoh is walking out to the water that morning, so Moses is told to be there when he comes. Moses is Israel’s leader, and I think he’s the only one in Egypt with a morning appointment like that.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.” It’s the very same staff that became a serpent in front of Pharaoh, friends. I’d be holding it a little more carefully than usual.

The answer is so they may worship Him in the wilderness. The LORD’s message says, “Let My people go, so that they may worship Me in the wilderness.” So the reason is worship, and it’s the LORD’s own word. The next line adds that until now Pharaoh has not listened.

The two answers are die and drink. The LORD says, “The fish in the Nile will die…” and also, “…the Egyptians will be unable to drink its water.” He says it ahead of time, and then it happens in verse 21. I think this one is heavy, and it’s worth sitting with for a second. Think of how many mornings start with a cup of something, and imagine the river itself saying no, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “There will be blood throughout the land of Egypt, even in the vessels of wood and stone.” So it’s not just the river, friends. It reaches the containers where people keep water too. Even my biggest mixing bowl wouldn’t be safe from that.

The answer is officials. The text says Aaron raised the staff and struck the water “in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials…” Pharaoh is Egypt’s king, and the officials are with him. Nobody could say they didn’t see it, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, “But the magicians of Egypt did the same things by their magic arts.” So they did match it, friends. Then Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.

The answer is that Pharaoh goes into his palace without taking it to heart. “Instead, Pharaoh turned around, went into his palace, and did not take any of this to heart.” He had just seen the whole river turn to blood and went straight inside, friends. I think that’s the quietest walk back to a building in the whole Bible.

The answer is that they dig around the Nile for it. “So all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water from the river.” ALL of them, digging, staring at the ground like it owes them something. I think that's what it looks like when nobody has a backup plan.
